stories.title: Israeli strike kills Hamas Rafah brigade commander Samir Abu Younis in Khan Younis
stories.summary: Hamas confirmed that Samir Abu Younis, commander of its Rafah brigade in the al-Qassam Brigades, was killed in an Israeli air strike on the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis in southern Gaza. The 53-year-old had been a member of the armed wing since 1991 and Israel described him as a key planner of the October 7, 2023 attack. His funeral was held in Khan Younis on Sunday afternoon.

stories.title: Philippines and Australia sign defence pact as South China Sea tensions flare
stories.summary: Australia and the Philippines signed a major defence cooperation agreement on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila, expanding reciprocal military access, maritime awareness and information sharing. The deal is expected to bolster the Philippine Navy and coastguard and covers eight new defence infrastructure projects at five sites. Canberra and Manila have both faced repeated clashes with Chinese forces in the disputed waters.

stories.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts missiles toward Riyadh and drones over Eastern Province
stories.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences intercepted and destroyed missiles launched toward Riyadh and drones over the kingdom’s Eastern Province. Spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said the coalition was responding to continued cross-border attacks as tensions with Yemen’s Houthi movement escalate. The coalition did not report casualties or damage in the latest interceptions.

stories.title: UN food agency chief calls for end to Sudan war as famine crisis deepens
stories.summary: The new executive director of the World Food Programme, Luke J. Lindberg, used a visit to the Goz Al-Salam camp for displaced people to call for an end to Sudan’s war and for more funding for humanitarian operations. Nearly 19.5 million people face acute food insecurity and about 825,000 children under five are expected to suffer severe acute malnutrition this year. The WFP says funding constraints forced it to cut assistance to 900,000 people and it is seeking $520 million to feed 5.4 million through April 2027.

stories.title: Tinubu breaks ground on $3.5bn Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu, represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, flagged off construction of the $3.5 billion Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State, a project delayed for years by political, legal and environmental disputes. The federal government said it completed environmental impact assessments and secured council approval with $2.27 billion in initial funding under a public-private partnership. Afreximbank is backing the project, which officials say will expand port capacity and support trade under the African Continental Free Trade Area.

stories.title: Naira depreciates to N1,445/$ in parallel market as gap with official rate widens to N86.50
stories.summary: The naira weakened to N1,445 per dollar in the parallel market, widening the spread with the official rate to about N86.50. The gap has persisted despite central bank efforts to unify exchange rates and attract foreign portfolio inflows. Analysts warn the divergence keeps pressure on import costs and complicates monetary policy ahead of the November MPC meeting.

stories.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global 365 outage hit Outlook, Teams and Copilot
stories.summary: Microsoft apologised and said it had restored service after a global outage that disrupted Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and Copilot for more than two workdays. Downdetector recorded reports from users in more than 70 countries, and governments, courts, hospitals, airlines and banks reported disruption. Microsoft said the incident stemmed from an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade and was not related to cyber activity or AI agents.

stories.title: Svitolina sets up WTA Finals title match against Andreeva at Indian Wells
stories.summary: Elina Svitolina reached the final of the 2026 WTA Finals at Indian Wells, where she will face Mirra Andreeva for the season-ending title. Svitolina, the 2018 champion, is playing the event for the first time since 2022, while Andreeva beat Jessica Pegula in the other semi-final to move one win from her first WTA Finals crown. The final closes the tournament on Sunday.

stories.title: 113th Grey Cup kicks off in Calgary as CFL crowns its champion
stories.summary: The 113th Grey Cup is being played at McMahon Stadium in Calgary, the sixth time the city has hosted the CFL championship and the first since 2019. The Montreal Alouettes clinched their place by beating the Winnipeg Blue Bombers in the East Division final. Sarah McLachlan performs the national anthem and Riley Green headlines the halftime show.

stories.title: New awards show celebrates AI music and the humans behind it
stories.summary: A new awards ceremony in Los Angeles has honoured AI-created songs and the people who make them, in an industry still divided over the technology. Organisers argue AI music is a new art form and a tool for creators, while critics point to lawsuits and complaints from artists whose work was used in training. The event drew nominees across genres and was livestreamed globally.

stories.title: WHO greenlights two Ebola Bundibugyo vaccine candidates for Phase 2/3 trials
stories.summary: The World Health Organization’s advisory group on candidate vaccine prioritisation has recommended Phase 2/3 trials for two vaccines targeting the Bundibugyo ebolavirus species driving the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The candidates are ChAdOx1 BDBV, developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna’s mRNA-1469. WHO science director Meg Doherty said trials could begin within three to four weeks once DRC regulators approve, with initial results expected in early 2027.

stories.title: Physicists use laser light to bring order to a crystal’s tiny electrical regions
stories.summary: Physicists at Auburn University have shown that brief flashes of laser light can align tiny electrically charged regions inside a crystal at temperatures where they would normally stay disordered. The induced order lasts about a trillionth of a second, and the team says it answers a decades-old question about how the material organises itself. The work points toward light-controlled approaches to processing and storing information.

stories.title: Rubin Observatory spots dwarf planet candidate 2026 ED138 far beyond Pluto
stories.summary: The NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory has identified 2026 ED138, a large, bright trans-Neptunian object that the International Astronomical Union’s Minor Planet Center has flagged as a dwarf planet candidate. The object is currently about 46 times farther from the Sun than Earth and takes roughly 281 years to complete an orbit, on a path tilted nearly 25 degrees to the plane of the solar system. If confirmed, it would rank among the largest dwarf planets found in that region.

stories.title: Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran strikes unless Tehran provokes US
stories.summary: President Donald Trump has told senior advisers in recent days that he may hold off on attacking Iran if Washington faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, according to three people familiar with the matter. Trump has alternated between threatening fresh strikes and signalling a wind-down, and officials say he does not appear to have made up his mind.

stories.title: US air travel slowly recovers after nationwide ground stop, with 10,000 flights hit
stories.summary: Airlines cancelled more than 5,300 US flights and delayed almost 6,300 on Saturday, a day after about 9,200 were cancelled when the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop over disrupted air traffic communications. The FAA head predicted schedules would not return to normal until late Sunday, and the transportation secretary is seeking $50 billion to upgrade air traffic control.

stories.title: SpaceX Starship returns to its Texas launch tower in first recovery of the spacecraft
stories.summary: SpaceX’s Starship came back from its longest flight in orbit yet and returned to the Texas launch tower it lifted off from a day earlier, the first key recovery of the rocket system’s centrepiece vessel. The flight was the 15th test of the two-stage vehicle and a milestone in the company’s decade-long effort to build a fully reusable rocket.

stories.title: Hundreds march in Bangui over fuel prices and the detention of five activists
stories.summary: Hundreds of demonstrators took to the streets of the Central African Republic’s capital to protest fuel price rises and demand the release of five civil society leaders arrested after an October strike. Petrol now costs more than 1,100 CFA francs a litre, and the opposition coalition behind the march wants it cut to 850.

stories.title: Dangote raises Africa investment ambition to $70bn and eyes a 10,000MW power push
stories.summary: Aliko Dangote has lifted his group’s planned investment in Africa from $50 billion to about $70 billion under its Vision 2030 strategy, with a separate 10,000-megawatt power programme across the continent that could include Nigeria. Captive generation for the group’s own plants is expected to rise from almost 1,500MW to between 4,500MW and 5,000MW.

stories.title: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10bn for the first time
stories.summary: OpenAI’s revenue passed $10 billion in the third quarter, according to Bloomberg-sourced reporting relayed by TechCrunch, an increase of almost 50% on the $6.7 billion booked in the previous quarter. The figures come from people familiar with the matter rather than company disclosures, and TechCrunch attached the caveat “if true”.

stories.title: Arokodare scores twice as Super Eagles bounce back with 3-1 win over Tanzania

Alphonce Msanga had equalised for Tanzania before Arokodare flicked home Wilfred Ndidi’s low ball and then smashed in Moses Usor’s cross.

stories.title: Rohr’s Benin go top of AFCON 2027 qualifying group after 4-1 win over CAR

stories.title: Lagos Art Week confronts history, identity and belonging at ART X Lagos
stories.summary: ART X Lagos, West Africa’s largest art fair, returned to the Federal Palace Hotel on Victoria Island as the centrepiece of Nigeria’s annual art week, with exhibitions, installations, music, talks and film screenings. This year’s edition, titled “A New Chapter, A New Decade”, explores how artists reinterpret heritage and identity.

stories.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases as MSF warns it is out of control
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has reported 10,741 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,230 deaths, with transmission active in eight provinces six months after the outbreak was declared. Médecins Sans Frontières warned on 12 November that the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record remains out of control, while WHO points to more than 2,600 recoveries and vaccine trials under way.

stories.title: Nigeria issues Addis Ababa travel advisory after 16 deaths in transit
stories.summary: Nigeria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has advised travellers with pre-existing medical conditions to seek medical advice before journeys through Addis Ababa, after the embassy there recorded 16 deaths of Nigerians in transit this year linked to the city’s high altitude. At about 2,355 metres, lower atmospheric pressure reduces oxygen availability, though the ministry stressed the advisory is not a call to avoid the city.

stories.summary: The decision to wind down the EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales. Elon Musk said the company will use the factory space to make more Cybercabs.

stories.summary: The WHO says DR Congo is recording 50 to 80 new Ebola cases daily, with the outbreak reaching 10,000 cases and nearly 5,000 deaths in six months.

stories.summary: The Federal Government has ordered 46 persons who had contact with an Ebola patient in Nigeria to be placed on a 21-day no-fly list to contain the virus.

stories.summary: A medical expert, Prof Oladapo Ashiru, has called for mandatory Ebola contact tracing for all travellers in Nigeria, with no VIP exemptions at airports.

stories.summary: NAFDAC has uncovered an illegal factory in Agege, Lagos, producing herbal bitters using a registration number belonging to a cough syrup.

stories.summary: The Nigerian Senate has urged the FG to release emergency funds and introduce mandatory health screening at all borders to curb the spread of Ebola.

stories.summary: Ogun State has intensified Ebola surveillance and traced 111 travellers after a case was announced in Abuja, the state's health commissioner has said.

stories.summary: They say Madhubalu, who lives in a Safari Park in Karachi, has improved somewhat but time will tell if all will be well.

stories.summary: The World Health Organisation has released new guidance to help governments and event organisers prevent and manage heat-related illnesses at mass gatherin

stories.title: Nigeria vaccinates 18 million girls against cervical cancer
stories.summary: The Nigerian government has vaccinated over 18 million adolescent girls against HPV, covering 76% of its target to eliminate cervical cancer.

stories.title: Wash dog bite for 15 minutes to prevent rabies, vet advises
stories.summary: A veterinary expert advises washing a dog bite with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes to prevent rabies before seeking medical attention.

stories.title: IRGC claims it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said its aerospace forces struck and destroyed a US early-warning radar installation in Bahrain, describing the operation as retaliation for an air strike on a telecommunications tower in the port town of Sirik. The claim was carried by IRGC-affiliated media and has not been independently verified; neither Washington nor Manama commented immediately. Bahrain issued a second alert of a potential threat as the exchange widened beyond the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Italy fines Meta €805m over access to Android users' photos
stories.summary: Italy's data protection authority fined Meta Platforms €805 million ($887 million) for using photos and videos from Android users' galleries on Facebook without specific consent or adequate disclosure. Investigators found the feature, which suggests gallery content for users to post, was enabled by default and covered by a single broad permission. Meta has 60 days to disable it by default and seek separate consent, and the company challenged Italy's jurisdiction.

stories.title: Philippines' Carmelle wins the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
stories.summary: Filipino singer Carmelle won the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Bangkok with a performance of her dance-pop song "Sobra-Sobra", taking 211 points. The 19-year-old beat 10 other acts in the grand final, with the result decided by national juries and viewers worldwide. A Thai duo finished second and Vietnam's Tóc Tiên third, as the 70-year-old contest expanded beyond Europe for the first time.

stories.title: Wales stun New Zealand 35-28 for first win over All Blacks since 1953
stories.summary: Wales beat New Zealand 35-28 in Cardiff for their first victory over the All Blacks in 73 years, built on tries from Tomos Williams, Dewi Lake, Archie Griffin, Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit. Wales led 21-7 at half-time before New Zealand cut the gap to seven, and the hosts repelled wave after wave of attack to hold on. It is one of the biggest upsets of the autumn internationals.

stories.title: Svitolina sets up WTA Finals title match against Andreeva
stories.summary: Elina Svitolina dropped just three games against Linda Noskova to reach the FAGE WTA Finals championship match at Indian Wells, while Mirra Andreeva knocked out Jessica Pegula to reach her first final. Andreeva had already beaten Svitolina in straight sets during group play, saving all six break points she faced. The final pits the world number three against a former champion chasing her biggest title in years.

stories.title: Portugal thrashed 4-1 by Denmark in first game since Ronaldo retired
stories.summary: Portugal lost 4-1 to Denmark in Braga in their first match since Cristiano Ronaldo announced his international retirement, with Rasmus Hojlund scoring twice in eight minutes early in the second half. Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg converted a penalty and Joachim Andersen headed a fourth before Bernardo Silva pulled one back in stoppage time. Every Portugal player and mascot wore 'Ronaldo 7' shirts in tribute before kick-off.

stories.title: Naira weakens to N1,445/$ in parallel market as official gap widens
stories.summary: The naira fell to N1,445 per dollar in the parallel market, down from N1,430 the previous day, widening the gap with the official window to N86.50. At the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market the currency actually firmed to N1,358.50/$, so the two rates moved in opposite directions. Bureau de Change operators in Abuja attributed the parallel pressure to demand that cannot be documented through official channels.

stories.title: New dinosaur species identified from near-complete South African skull
stories.summary: Paleontologists have named Nyana rooiwalensis, a dinosaur that lived about 220 million years ago in what is now South Africa's Eastern Cape, from a 21.3cm juvenile skull found near Qhemegha village in 2018. Despite being roughly three years old the animal already weighed about 400kg and walked on two legs, suggesting rapid growth arose early in sauropodomorph evolution. The find is one of the most complete dinosaur skulls from this period on the southern continents.

stories.title: South Africa faces coalition talks in 136 municipalities after local elections
stories.summary: South Africa's electoral commission declared the 2026 local government elections free and fair, with the ANC on 30.76% nationally and 3,246 council seats, followed by the DA on 24.64% and the MK Party on 9.76%. Only 74 of 213 municipalities produced an outright majority, leaving 136 needing coalition arrangements, including the metros of Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni. President Cyril Ramaphosa said political differences should not stand in the way of cooperation.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass in remote Andes town he once served
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV travelled by helicopter to Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, a town of about 5,000 people in the Andean highlands of the diocese where he served as bishop from 2015 to 2023. In his homily at an open-air Mass he praised the missionaries who evangelised the region and the popular piety of the high Andes. The visit is part of his apostolic journey through Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

stories.title: Zimbabwe's HIV gains face their hardest test among young people
stories.summary: Zimbabwe has exceeded the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets, with 97% of people living with HIV aware of their status, more than 95% on antiretroviral therapy and 96% of those virally suppressed. But critical gaps remain for children, adolescents and pregnant women, and nearly half of adolescents and young people are not in education, employment or training. Awareness of HIV status among young people in Harare rose from 63% to 85% between August 2025 and September 2026.

stories.title: Fani-Kayode presents credentials to Ramaphosa as Nigeria-South Africa envoy
stories.summary: Femi Fani-Kayode has formally assumed duty as Nigeria's ambassador to South Africa after presenting his letter of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa. He pledged to rebuild relations between Abuja and Pretoria, which have been strained by diplomatic friction in recent months. The ceremony was reported by Nigerian outlets including Premium Times and ThisDay.

stories.title: Turkey and Qatar sign mutual defence agreement in Doha
stories.summary: Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani signed a mutual defence pact aimed at strengthening collective defence and regional security. The two leaders also signed agreements covering trade, energy, diplomacy, education and culture. The visit came as Gulf states weigh their response to Israel's war in Gaza and efforts to normalise Syria.

stories.title: Marcos opens 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila with 19 leaders expected
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr chaired the opening of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City. The three-day meeting under the theme 'Navigating Our Future, Together' covers regional security, economic resilience and the bloc's response to the crisis in Myanmar. Marcos is due to hand the ASEAN chairship to Singapore at the close.

stories.title: France mobilises 70,000 police for fifth weekend of protests
stories.summary: Between 50 and 60 marches were expected across France as the 'Yellow Vests' coordination and student unions held a fifth consecutive weekend of demonstrations over the cost of living, education funding and a new police bill. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez mobilised around 70,000 police officers and gendarmes, with the Paris march running from Place de la Republique to Place de la Nation. The movement has produced thousands of arrests since it began in mid-October.

stories.title: South Sudan postpones first national elections to February 2027
stories.summary: South Sudan's National Election Commission published a revised timetable setting 11 February 2027 as polling day, replacing 22 December 2026, on the day voter registration was due to begin. The document gave no reason for the delay, which follows warnings from the South Sudan Civil Society Forum that conditions did not support fair and credible elections. The vote, the country's first since independence in 2011, has now been deferred repeatedly, including in 2022 and 2024.

stories.title: Burkina Faso issues arrest warrants for journalists and ex-minister
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's Ouagadougou Court of Appeal issued arrest warrants for around 20 people in exile, including RFI journalist Newton Ahmed Barry and former foreign minister Djibril Bassole. Attorney General Desire Sawadogo said 14 warrants carried extradition requests alongside seven standard warrants, with charges including complicity in forming and financing a terrorist organisation. The junta, in power since September 2022, has repeatedly targeted journalists and critics.

stories.title: Tinubu pledges to rebuild violence-ravaged Plateau communities
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu used a campaign stop in Jos to promise the reconstruction of communities displaced by years of violence in Plateau State. He said his administration's reforms were beginning to stabilise the economy and asked residents of the North-Central zone for a second term. Information Minister Mohammed Idris said the turnout reflected confidence in the government's programme.

stories.title: S&P 500 ends volatile week at 7,561 as Nvidia slide deepens
stories.summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,561.53 on Friday, capping a week in which investors weighed a hotter inflation reading against fresh uncertainty over Nvidia's leadership. The Dow added about 0.1% while the Nasdaq was roughly flat, and the 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.17%, its highest since October. Nvidia shares fell 2% to $162.85 ahead of the chipmaker's earnings this week.

stories.title: Reuters finds $3.2bn of Chinese AI projects built on restricted Nvidia chips
stories.summary: A Reuters review of more than 150 Chinese procurement notices, investment plans and corporate filings identified AI computing projects worth over 23 billion yuan, about $3.2 billion, specifying Nvidia's restricted H100, H200 and H800 processors. Nvidia told investors in August that US export controls had effectively shut it out of China's data-centre market, yet an IDC estimate cited by Reuters put its share of Chinese AI accelerator shipments at 34% in the first half of 2026. The records do not establish how the restricted hardware reached Chinese users.

stories.title: Notre Dame routs Boston College 41-7 in South Bend
stories.summary: Fifth-ranked Notre Dame beat Boston College 41-7 in the latest edition of the Holy War, with the Fighting Irish offence scoring on the ground and through the air. Boston College's lone score came on a third-quarter rushing touchdown by Bo MacCormack III, and defensive back KP Price recorded an interception and a sack. Notre Dame improved to 8-1 with the win.

stories.title: NC State hires Philip Rivers as head football coach
stories.summary: NC State named former Wolfpack and NFL quarterback Philip Rivers as its next head coach on a five-year deal, after its board of trustees approved the contract. Rivers, 44, replaces Dave Doeren, who was fired in October, and takes his first college coaching job after leading St Michael Catholic in Alabama since 2021. He will be introduced at a private event on Monday that airs on the ACC Network.

stories.title: Recording Academy sets 16 November for 2027 Grammy nominations
stories.summary: The Recording Academy will reveal nominees for the 69th Grammy Awards on Monday, 16 November, in a presentation streamed on Grammy.com and the Grammys YouTube channel with live coverage on Good Morning America. Pharrell Williams, Herbie Hancock, Kehlani, Olivia Dean, David Guetta and Ziggy Marley are among the artists announcing categories. The 2027 ceremony, set for 7 February, adds five new categories including best Asian pop music performance.

stories.title: South Africa pushes early diabetes detection on World Diabetes Day
stories.summary: Hundreds of Johannesburg residents received free blood pressure and diabetes screenings as South Africa marked World Diabetes Day under the theme 'Early action on diabetes'. Diabetes is the country's leading underlying natural cause of death, claiming nearly 29,000 lives a year, and roughly one in nine South African adults lives with the condition. The WHO says more than 40% of people with diabetes worldwide are undiagnosed.

stories.title: Voyager 1 to become first human-made object one light-day from Earth
stories.summary: NASA says Voyager 1 will cross the one-light-day threshold on Wednesday, 18 November, at 5:16 a.m. EST, roughly 16 billion miles from Earth. The spacecraft, launched in 1977, will have taken 49 years, two months and 11 days to cover a distance light itself crosses in 24 hours. After that milestone a radio command takes about 24 hours to reach it, and a reply another 24 to return.
